conflicts.what: If update_options validates every acme_url it is given, the store_account write-back (lemur/plugins/lemur_acme/acme_handlers.py:220-237) re-persists a legacy authority's stored acme_url and would start raising. Issuance would then break for legacy authorities documented as trusted (plugin.py:38-39). The check must stay on user-supplied writes or on changed values only.

Validating directory_url at the fetch site to catch an override would also reject the config fallback (lemur/tests/conf.py:216, not allowlisted) and legacy stored rows. Only the override value may be checked.

A natural check written as option['name'] == 'acme_url', or one gated on a list-of-dicts shape, raises on the existing PUT test payload [{'updated': 'bar'}] (lemur/tests/test_authorities.py:438). Use option.get('name') and leave non-acme options alone.

fairness_risks: The allowlist requires https (plugin.py:50), but the ACME plugin option regex accepts http:// (plugin.py:72, :369). A hidden test that PUTs a legitimate http internal ACME URL would expect rejection, which matches create-time behaviour but contradicts the documented option format.

The default allowlist (plugin.py:43-47) does not contain the test-config fallback acme-v01.api.letsencrypt.org (lemur/tests/conf.py:216). Any rule enforced at the fetch site or on the config fallback breaks existing handler tests (test_acme_dns.py:264-279).

PUT options is a free-form string (schemas.py:101). The existing test stores entries without a 'name' key (test_authorities.py:438), so a rule requiring a well-formed plugin-option list rejects a shape that a legitimate use still needs.
update_options must keep accepting cab_compliant-only option lists (test_certificates.py:249, :264) and the store_account write-back of legacy rows (acme_handlers.py:221-237).

design.why: T1 is the advisory route the report points at. The same fix must also cover T2 (every acme_url entry) and keep T3 working (entries without 'name', non-ACME authorities). T4 is a deepseek-type trap: protection absent, with a strong 'internal only' reason to dismiss. It needs T6's planted caller to be externally reachable, and then T4+T6 count as one group. T5 is a mimo-type coupled value: the config fallback and legacy rows must still reach the fetch, which punishes validating at the sink. T7 is a planted per-request override that must be validated without breaking T5. That gives four groups with different reasons to dismiss (none; internal-only; documented legacy trust; trusted-config merge) and two real conflicts (T4/T5, T7/T5). Without injection the pinned code has only one externally reachable group (T1) plus an unreachable writer (T4), which is too thin to stack.
